title: Introduction to NFL Analytics with R
name: Expected Points Added (EPA) as pre/post-play EP difference
quote: At its core, EPA is the difference in expected points before and after each play. Because of this, on any given play, a team has the ability to either increase or decrease the expected points, with EPA being that specific difference. Importantly, EPA includes various contextual factors into its calculation such as down, distance, position on the field, etc. Then, based on historical data, an estimation of how many points, on average, a team is expected to score on a given situation is provided.
section: Appendix A.9 Expected Points Added (EPA), printed p338

title: Introduction to NFL Analytics with R
name: Completion Percentage Over Expected (CPOE) as context-adjusted completion
quote: At the conclusion fo the 2016 season, Sam Bradford, the quarterback of the Minnesota Vikings, recorded the highest completion percentage in NFL history, connecting on 71.6% of his attempts during the season. However, Bradford achieved this record by averaging just 6.4 yards per attempt. Bradford's recordbreaking completion percentage is suddenly less impressive when one realizes that he was rarely attempting downfield passes.
section: Appendix A.6 Completion Percentage Over Expected (CPOE), printed pp334-335

title: Introduction to NFL Analytics with R
name: Success rate: historical yardage thresholds vs modern EPA>0 predicate
quote: Prior to the formulation of EP and EPA, success rate was calculated based on the percentage of yardage gained on a play (40% of the necessary yards on 1st down, 60% on 2nd down, and 100% of the yards needed for a 1st down on both 3rd and 4th downs). However, modern success rate is determined simply by whether or not the specific play had an EPA greater than 0.
section: Appendix A.13 Success Rate, printed p343

title: Introduction to NFL Analytics with R
name: xYAC Success: probability a reception yields positive EPA after catch
quote: Just as above XYAC Success is the probability that the reception results in a positive EPA, xYAC Mean Yardage is the expected yards after catch based on where the ball was caught.
section: Appendix A.10-A.11 xYAC Success / xYAC Mean Yardage, printed p340

title: Introduction to NFL Analytics with R
name: Running back efficiency: NextGen distance traveled per yard gained
quote: A running back's efficiency is measured by taking the total distance traveled, according to NextGen Stats, per the total of yards gained on the run. A lower number indicates a more North/South type runner, while a higher number indicates a running back that "dances" and runs laterally relevant to the line of scrimmage.
section: Appendix A.8 Running Back Efficiency, printed p337
